Correlation test between x and y, partial if covariates are given

Source: R/cor_pair.R
partial_cor_test.Rd

  • no covariate: stats::cor.test() (exact = FALSE);

  • covariates: ppcor::pcor.test() (default engine); fallback or engine = "base": correlation of the residuals of x and y on Z (for Spearman x, y AND Z are ranked, as in ppcor), t-test with n - 2 - k df. For Pearson this is exactly the slope test of lm(y ~ x + Z) (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem). Kendall partial correlations need ppcor.

partial_rank_cor() is the former name, kept for backward compatibility.

Usage

partial_cor_test(
  x,
  y,
  Z = NULL,
  meth = c("spearman", "pearson", "kendall"),
  engine = c("ppcor", "base"),
  ci = 0.95
)

partial_rank_cor(x, y, Z = NULL, meth = c("spearman", "pearson"))

Arguments

x, y

numeric vectors (binary: 0/1, see as_cor_numeric())

Z

data frame of covariates (factors allowed: dummy coded) or NULL

meth

"spearman" (ranks), "pearson" (values) or "kendall"

engine

"ppcor" (default) or "base" (residual method)

ci

confidence level of the interval (NULL = none); Fisher z on n - k

Value

list(estimate, p.value, n, k, ci_low, ci_high, engine, ci_engine)

Examples

d <- simulate_cor_data(100)
partial_cor_test(d$IL6, d$fatigue, meth = "spearman")
#> $estimate
#> [1] 0.5246237
#> 
#> $p.value
#> [1] 5.712139e-08
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 94
#> 
#> $k
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $ci_low
#> [1] 0.3550094
#> 
#> $ci_high
#> [1] 0.6607999
#> 
#> $engine
#> [1] "stats::cor.test"
#> 
#> $ci_engine
#> [1] "correlation::cor_to_ci"
#> 
partial_cor_test(d$NfL, d$cognition, Z = d[, c("age", "sex")], meth = "pearson")
#> $estimate
#> [1] -0.04689676
#> 
#> $p.value
#> [1] 0.6571061
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 94
#> 
#> $k
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $ci_low
#> [1] -0.2493194
#> 
#> $ci_high
#> [1] 0.1594522
#> 
#> $engine
#> [1] "ppcor::pcor.test"
#> 
#> $ci_engine
#> [1] "correlation::cor_to_ci"
#>
